subject: Private deployment cryptographic custodianship & HSM/BYOK architecture review
messages:
From: Jack Morrison <jack.morrison@acme-fin.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: security_ops@acme-fin.com
Date: 2026-05-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: BYOK / HSM custodianship model for private deploy

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we scope the VPC/private deployment for our regulated workloads, the security team needs a short architecture review focused on key custodianship and encryption boundaries. Specifically we need to confirm: 

- Can Redwood support BYOK where we maintain root keys (KMS CMKs) in our HSM and only import wrapped DEKs for runtime?
- What HSM models/attestation are supported (PKCS#11, Nitro, Thales Luna) and do you have FIPS level guidance?
- How does rotation work end-to-end (who rotates, how are old keys retired, emergency revoke)?
- Network segmentation requirements: can HSMs live in a dedicated subnet with strict egress rules and TLS mutual auth to Redwood agents?

We have a short audit next month and would appreciate a one-page summary + any diagrams you can share. Also please note we may involve Thales for an integration call — looping them in is fine.

Thanks,
Jack
Jack Morrison
Dir, Cloud Security - Acme Financial

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-20T17:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK / HSM custodianship model for private deploy

Jack — thanks for the clear ask. I prepared a concise design summary and attached a one-page blueprint (Redwood_Key_Design_Blueprint_v1.pdf) illustrating the recommended approach for private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. High-level answers below; I'll add details and a diagram in the attachment.

Summary answers (short):
- BYOK model: yes — we support an envelope encryption pattern where customer-managed CMKs live in a customer-controlled HSM (BYOK). Redwood receives only wrapped Data Encryption Keys (DEKs). We support both import of externally-wrapped DEKs (bring-wrapped-key) and a remote-wrap flow where Redwood generates a DEK and the customer KMS wraps it under their CMK using an attested TLS session.

- HSM compatibility: we support any HSM exposing PKCS#11 or a vendor API for key import/export (Thales, Luna, Gemalto, Nitro HSM variants). For regulated workloads we recommend a FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or FIPS 140-3 L2+ HSM depending on threat model; we can provide specific test matrices.

- Rotation model: preferred pattern is staggered rotation — rotate DEKs frequently (e.g., 30–90 days) and CMKs less frequently (annual or per-policy). Key retirement uses a tombstone period (configurable, recommended 90 days) with automatic rewrap of live artifacts. Emergency revoke: we support immediate blacklisting of CMKs/WRAPPED keys and cross-region fallback to a verified Redwood-managed key only under documented, auditable emergency governance.

- Network & segmentation: HSMs can reside in a dedicated private subnet peered to Redwood agents over a customer-managed transit (VPC peering/PrivateLink/VPN). Minimum egress is mTLS to Redwood agent IPs on port 443 and SSH for maintenance (optional). We recommend isolating HSM management plane to jump-hosts with MFA and IP allowlists.

Next steps:
1) I'll schedule an architecture review call with Vivek (runtime lead) and Mina (security) to walk through the blueprint.
2) If helpful, we can invite Thales to confirm the import/wrap flows.

Attaching: Redwood_Key_Design_Blueprint_v1.pdf (diagram + steps).

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BYOK / HSM custodianship model for private deploy

Jack / Priya — a few operational notes from the runtime and infra perspective: 

- Envelope encryption: we recommend DEKs be AES-256-GCM with associated metadata that includes key id, version, and epoch. DEKs should be ephemeral in agent memory (never persisted unwrapped) and protected with a hardware-backed key-encryption-key (KEK) provided by the customer CMK.

- Attestation & import: for the remote-wrap flow, we use a mutual-TLS + attestation token exchange (TPM/attest agent) to verify the agent before requesting a wrap. For bring-wrapped-key, the HSM must export a wrapped key blob that conforms to a PKCS#11-wrapped format (or CMS/WrappedData) that we can ingest. If Thales requires a vendor-specific envelope we can add a small adapter.

- HSM network: put HSMs in a management subnet with no internet egress; all wrapping/unwrapping calls are initiated from the agents inside your VPC via a private peering link. Agents talk to the HSM over the vendor-specific protocol (e.g., 2050/TCP for Luna, or PKCS#11 over socket). We will ship a hardened agent (FIPS-mode TLS stacks) and can pin ciphers.

- Logging & audit: Redwood will produce KMS audit events (key-id, operation, agent-id, request-id, timestamps) and we can forward those logs to your SIEM over the private link. If you require HSM-audit retention, we recommend retaining HSM syslogs for 1 year (configurable).

- Backup & escrow: we recommend a split-knowledge key-escrow for CMKs used for emergency unwrap. Escrow should be stored in a different physical region and require multi-person approval.

I attached a quick network sketch (hsm-network-segmentation-diagram.png) and noted a couple of items we should validate with Thales: support for remote-wrap API and whether offline key ceremony/import is needed for their appliance.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Runtime, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is good. A couple of security-specific clarifications we need before the audit: 

1) Rotation SLA and signal: please spell out who triggers CMK rotation vs DEK rotation. My preference is: customer triggers CMK rotation (we can automate rewrap), Redwood triggers DEK rotation based on token volume/time (configurable), and both events emit a KMS event that we can ingest into your SIEM.

2) Key life cycle states: please confirm state transitions (Active -> Pending-Retire -> Retired -> Destroyed) and timelines. We need the ability to freeze/rollback a rotation within a 24–48 hour window in case of a regression to model behavior.

3) Attestation & proof of possession: for any remote-wrap flow we require a signed attestation token from the agent including firmware hash + agent version. If the HSM supports it, we also want an HSM-signed nonce proving the CMK is within a certified boundary.

4) Secrets handling in CI/CD: we need a recommended workflow for provisioning agent config and wrapped keys into CI/CD (GitHub Actions / Jenkins). Prefer ephemeral secrets via a sealed secret store (Vault / sealed-secrets) and avoid storing wrapped keys in plaintext in repos.

Can you update the blueprint with: a short lifecycle table, attestation sample, and recommended CI/CD pattern?

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr Manager, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
